summary: Describes how a SIP response can carry a Q.850 cause code in a Reason header field. Some deployments already did this for failures on calls gatewayed to the phone network, and this document writes down the practice formally. It is a standards-track specification.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC specifies how SIP responses can carry Q.850 cause codes in a Reason header. It allows a response to include the telephone-network cause, except for the 100 Trying response.

questions: how are q850 codes carried in sip
can a sip trying response include q850 reason
how should the sip reason header be protected
subtitle: A way for SIP responses to carry Q.850 cause codes in the Reason header.

tldr.problem: SIP's Reason header had no specified use for Q.850 failure causes, even though systems were already using it for gatewayed calls.
tldr.mechanism: A SIP response other than 100 Trying MAY include a Reason header with a Q.850 cause code.
tldr.outcome: The RFC formalizes this use and recommends integrity protection to prevent a false cause code.

facts.label: Responses that may include the field

today: RFC 6432 is a Proposed Standard. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Passing Telephone-Network Causes
sections.content:
RFC 3326 describes the SIP Reason header generally but does not specify it for particular response codes. Systems gatewaying SIP INVITE requests to the public switched telephone network were already using the header to carry Q.850 failure-related cause codes.

This RFC formally describes that use in SIP responses.
sections.plainLanguage: Systems were already placing telephone-network failure codes in SIP responses. This document writes down how to use the Reason header for those codes.

sections.title: Where the Reason Header May Appear
sections.content:
Any SIP response except 100 (Trying) MAY contain a Reason header with a Q.850 cause code. The RFC excludes 100 Trying because it is sent hop by hop rather than end to end.

Reason values other than Q.850 cause codes are outside this document's scope.
sections.plainLanguage: Most SIP responses may carry the Q.850 cause. The short-lived 100 Trying response is excluded because it is not sent end to end.

sections.title: Integrity Protection
sections.content:
A wrong Q.850 cause code could lead to an announcement system playing incorrect information. The RFC RECOMMENDS protecting the Reason header with a suitable integrity mechanism.

Transport-layer TLS or network-layer IPsec with appropriate cipher suites can provide the required protection.
sections.plainLanguage: A changed cause code could lead a system to give the wrong explanation. Integrity protection helps detect or prevent that change.

references.text: Schulzrinne, H., Oran, D., and G. Camarillo, "The Reason Header Field for the Session Initiation Protocol (SIP)", RFC 3326, December 2002.
